title: Enforce MCP config/hooks file gitignore parity via fresh-checkout regression test
context: .windsurf/hooks.json was committed while .windsurf/mcp_config.json was gitignored, breaking the established pattern for every other harness (.cursor, .codex, .agents). This caused `hunch doctor` to detect a harness with a missing config on every fresh clone, failing CI unconditionally.
decision: Added .windsurf/hooks.json to .gitignore and deleted it from tracking. Added a regression test that reconstructs a fresh checkout from git-tracked files and asserts `hunch doctor` passes, catching gitignore asymmetries before they break CI.
consequences: Fresh clones now pass `hunch doctor` unconditionally (CI unblocked)
Regression test guards against similar harness config asymmetries in the future
Windsurf config pattern now matches every other harness (MCP config + hooks file gitignored as a pair)
Test uses the repository's own tracked files, making the check self-documenting and impossible to drift from reality
alternatives_rejected: Fix only the gitignore without regression test — leaves pattern vulnerable to repeat mistakes
Commit .windsurf/mcp_config.json instead — violates principle that per-developer harness configs should not be tracked
Make `hunch doctor` lenient toward missing MCP configs — hides real configuration problems
